newsitem.title: USA: N.H. retailers attack proposed cigarette tax hike.
newsitem.headline: N.H. retailers attack proposed cigarette tax hike.

text.p: New Hampshire retailers and House Speaker attacked Gov. Jeanne Shaheen's proposed hike in the state's tax on cigarettes to 25 cents per pack Thursday, saying it would hurt the state's cigarette sales.

A New Hampshire Retail Merchants Association lobbyist told reporters at the state house that his group opposes any increase. It will hurt "Mom and Pop" stores in border communities that depend on out-of-state customers who come to buy cigarettes and also purchase such other products as beer and groceries, the lobbyist said.
Shaheen has proposed hiking the tax to 25 cents from 11 cents a pack to pay for a statewide kindergarten program.
New Hampshire is the only state that does not require kindergarten education. It began funding a limited program last year and Shaheen wants to provide more money for it.
Meanwhile, House Speaker Donna Sytek told reporters she was skeptical that a tax hike would pass muster in the Republican-dominated House.

New Hampshire's current tax on cigarettes yields more than $45 million to the state treasury annually. The state offers the cheapest cigarette prices of all New England states. Critics of the tax increase say it will hurt sales and hamper revenue growth.

While Shaheen has not formally proposed a specific tax amount yet, state Department of Revenue Administration Commissioner Stanley Arnold has projected revenue from a tax increase ranging from 12 cents to 25 cents a pack.

Arnold said a 20 cent per pack increase would keep New Hampshire cigarette prices below its closest New England competitor and provide significant income. Arnold said a 20 cent per pack increase would not discourage hurting sales.
Shaheen said a tax increase between 11 and 25 cents per pack will bring in "substantial revenues" and lose just a small percentage of sales.
New Hampshire's 25 cents per pack tax is well below Vermont's 51 cents, Maine's 48 cents and Massachusetts' 86 cents per pack taxes.
